properties.name: Khorog - Pamir Highway and Wakhan (Tajikistan) [no lift]

description.value:
Remote high-altitude mountain-bike expeditions through the Pamirs

Trails
Khorog is the main riding and logistics base for the Pamir Highway, Wakhan Valley and Gorno-Badakhshan. This is expedition terrain rather than a trail centre: long gravel stages cross passes above 4,000 m, with rough descents including Koi-Tezek, Nayzatash and Ak-Baital. Side valleys add unmaintained tracks, river crossings and very isolated mountain riding.

Getting up / price
No lift. Most trips combine pedalling with a 4x4 support vehicle, luggage transport and local guiding. Independent riding is possible for experienced expedition cyclists, but distances, altitude and limited supplies make supported travel strongly advisable.

Open season
Open from 01 July; closed from 01 October (average high-pass riding window).
Daily opening hours: daylight hours
A GBAO permit is required. Some border areas and Zorkul require additional permission; rules, crossings and road conditions can change at short notice.

Access
FromTransportDuration
KhorogBike / 4x4Direct
DushanbeFlight / long 4x4 transferVariable

Sources: Travel to Tajikistan sports tourism, the Pamir Guides bike-tour itinerary and Travel Tajikistan Pamir Highway itinerary. Confirm permits, security advice and current road access before departure.

Natural Tian Shan enduro and adventure riding above Charvak Reservoir

Trails
Chimgan is the main mountain base near Tashkent, with rocky jeep tracks, shepherd paths, gorge descents and steep natural terrain in the Ugam-Chatkal mountains. It is best approached as a guided backcountry ride rather than a maintained bike park; trail marking and reliable difficulty information are limited.

Getting up / price
Pedal access or locally arranged vehicle support. No operating mountain-bike lift is documented. Nearby Amirsoy runs gondolas for sightseeing, but its official summer activity information does not confirm bicycle carriage.

Open season
Open from 01 May; closed from 01 November (average snow-free riding season).
Daily opening hours: daylight hours
Confirm the route, protected-area rules and any permit requirements with a local guide before riding.

Sources: Amirsoy official activities and Visit Tashkent mountain-area information. Current MTB infrastructure is not formally documented, so verify locally.

Community-based natural mountain biking in the eastern Tian Shan

Trails
Marked village routes include the 7 km Tulpar Tash ride, the 13 km Kok-Bel waterfall route and the 16.6 km Eki Chat loop. Stronger riders can tackle the rough Kok-Bel Pass route, with alpine terrain, river valleys and technical natural sections. Local guesthouses arrange rentals and guides.

Getting up / price
Pedal access; no lift. Guided rides and vehicle support can be arranged locally. The destination lists bike rental at 1,320 KGS per day or 660 KGS per half day; confirm current rates.

Open season
Open from 01 June; closed from 01 October (official recommended riding season is June to September).
Daily opening hours: daylight hours
Mountain weather changes quickly. Carry repair and navigation equipment, and use a local guide for remote routes.

Natural Tian Shan enduro and multi-day riding hub

Trails
Karakol is the principal base for forest singletrack, alpine valleys and long natural descents around Jeti-Oguz and the eastern Issyk-Kul region. Riding ranges from approachable valley routes to remote high-pass adventures with substantial climbing and exposed mountain terrain.

Getting up / price
Pedal access or a locally arranged shuttle; no lift-served bike park is documented. Do not assume that nearby ski lifts carry bicycles. Karakol has bike rental and guiding operators for day rides and supported multi-day trips.

Open season
Open from 01 June; closed from 15 October (average high-country riding season).
Daily opening hours: daylight hours
Route conditions and river crossings vary. A guide is strongly recommended outside the lower valley network.

properties.name: St-Cergue / La Dôle (Jura vaudois) [train fare only]

description.value:
La Givrine (top of the NStCM train)

Trails
The closest real singletrack riding to Lausanne. Three marked descents drop off the Jura crest back towards Arzier and St-Cergue: Mont Chaubert, Mont Bailly (plus an eastern variant) and La Plagne. Rooty, rocky, north-facing forest trails, short (1-2 km each) but you can chain them and pedal back up in 20-30 min, or reload with the train. Dry quickly, ridable from April to November - the best shoulder-season option on this map.

Getting up / price
No lift needed: the train is the climb (Nyon 400 m > La Givrine 1228 m). Normal CFF/NStCM fare, plus a bike ticket - the national day bike pass is about 14 CHF (bikes are carried on the NStCM, space is limited at peak times).

Open season
Open from 1 April; closed from 1 December (typical window; check the operator and conditions).

Chaumont - top of the La Coudre funicular

Trails
Chaumont bike park: a proper DH line with 110+ doubles and around 20 drops, clearly aimed at experienced riders - but a chicken line runs alongside the whole way so you can pick your level. Back down to La Coudre it alternates forest doubletrack and singletrack. Open all year, which makes it the winter fallback when the Alps are shut.

The funicular is part of the Neuchatel city network (transN / Onde Verte): a few francs per ride, so this is by far the cheapest lift-served riding in the region. Runs year-round, every 15-30 min.

Berneuse 2048 m - top of the Leysin gondola

Trails
Leysin Bike Park, still young and still growing. Two machine-built runs off the Berneuse: Nerine (1 km, red/black) and Les 3 Tours (0.4 km, red/black), plus a short liaison between them - steep, rocky and aimed at confident riders. A blue intermediate line is due in August 2026 and a green one in 2027. Off-park, the Endless Ride enduro descent towards Prafandaz and Roc de Veyges is the reason to come, and stage 1 of the Alpes du Leman Bike route runs from here to Les Diablerets.

Getting up / price
Gondola + downhill day pass around 28 CHF. Free with the Magic Pass. Bike park opens 25 April 2026, daily 20 June - 23 August, weekends either side; the Tete d'Ai chairlift runs 11:30-16:00 in high summer.

Open season

Rochers de Naye 2042 m - top station

Trails
The biggest single descent reachable from Lausanne in under 90 minutes: 1500 m of vertical from 2042 m down to the lake. Mostly moderately technical alpine singletrack, several variants (the La Perche line is the classic), then forest trails through Caux and Glion back to Montreux. Exposed and rocky up top - not a beginner run, and not much fun in the wet.

Getting up / price
Montreux > Rochers-de-Naye return is 70 CHF full fare / 35 CHF with a half-fare card. A cheaper ascent-only day ticket for bikers and paragliders (around 39 CHF) has been offered in past seasons. Bike capacity on the rack train is genuinely limited - call MVR ahead rather than turning up with three mates.

⚠️ Only ride on single tracks that are marked for biking, or carrosable, as this is Vaud canton.

Open season
Open from 1 May; closed from 1 November (typical window; check the operator and conditions).

Beyond the park, Freeride Grand Montana and the Montana-Village > Loc flowtrail give you long natural descents through the larch forest all the way to the valley.

Trails
The Grand Chamossaire descent, opened in summer 2025: 3 km of blue flow with big berms, a few technical sections and smooth fast bits between them - built for families and improving riders rather than for hucking. Around it sits a dense network of marked SuisseMobile routes: 573 Bretaye > Villars, 572 Bretaye > Ollon (a long 20 km+ descent to the Rhone valley), 580 towards Les Chaux and Solalex, and 582 Taveyanne-Solalex. Villars also preserves the Maxi Avalanche line toward the valley, with roughly 1500 m of vertical from the Roc d'Orsay sector.

properties.name: Bienne / Magglingen - BielTrail [16 CHF with Half Fare]

description.value:
Magglingen/Macolin - top of the funicular

Trails
BielTrail is a 1.95 km, 440 m descent running point-to-point back towards the funicular. Most of the main line is fast, flowing and well maintained, but it includes a short black section that is genuinely technical: a steep downhill passage through rocks and roots. Additional, more relaxed paths descend through the same area, but these are shared with hikers rather than bike-only trails: slow down, give way and expect people around blind corners. The wider Jura network (Les Pres-d'Orvin Bike 844, Erguel Bike 843) starts from the same plateau if you want more distance.

Getting up / price
The Magglingen funicular is part of Biel city transport. A day costs 16 CHF with the Swiss Half Fare Travelcard, making repeated laps unusually good value. There is a bike wash behind the lower funicular station.

Open season
Open from 1 January with no seasonal closure in a typical year; avoid riding when the ground is saturated and check local conditions.

The gateway to 600 km of marked MTB trails and 21 open lifts - the biggest lift-linked bike area within reach of Lausanne. From Planachaux you can ride the whole loop into France (Chatel, Morzine, Les Gets, Avoriaz) on one pass - the Pass'Portes weekend, 26-28 June 2026, is the day to do it.

Trails
Switzerland's most serious bike destination, and a UCI World Cup venue - the 2026 round is 19-21 June. The Bike Kingdom Park runs five parallel lines off the same lift so you can pick your level and lap all day: FLOWline (green, wide and rolling), PRIMEline and SHOREline in the middle, STYLEline for jumps, and STRAIGHTline, the steep, fast World Cup track. Beyond the park, the Biketicket to RIDE network and the Bike Attack race line drop the full 1400 m off the Rothorn. Big Skill Centre at the Rothorn valley station for a warm-up.

Getting up / price
Bike Kingdom day ticket from 53 CHF, about 6% less booked online. One ticket covers Lenzerheide, Arosa and Chur, and bike carriage is included on every lift. Multi-day tickets and the Gravity Card season pass are the sensible options if you stay.

Enormous: 45 routes over roughly 300 km of marked trail and 2610 m of vertical from the Pic Blanc at 3330 m down to 1450 m. Alpe d'Huez is the venue of Megavalanche, the iconic mass start race that launches riders together from the Pic Blanc glacier into a marathon descent to Allemond. The built lines around the resort cover everything - Marmotland and Easy Rider for beginners, the Rif Nel flow trail and Central Park for jumps, Hot Road and Run DMC when you want speed. Above them sits a high-alpine descent that is genuinely one of the longest in Europe.

Whistler Mountain Bike Park (British Columbia) [season pass 999 CAD]

description.value:
Fitzsimmons Express top 1020 m - the bike park's main unload

Trails
The one every other bike park is measured against. Around eighty machine-built and natural trails over four zones: Fitzsimmons for the famous flow - A-Line, Dirt Merchant, Crank It Up - Garbanzo above it for longer and steeper, Creekside for the quiet side, and the Peak zone for Top of the World, a high alpine descent of roughly 1500 m. Green jump lines through to double-black tech, and the trail crew rebuilds constantly. Oukaimeden plateau, about 2600 m - High Atlas natural enduro

Trails
A high-altitude base for raw, unmarked descents on mule trails, goat paths and old village tracks rather than a maintained bike park. Guided rides link jeep tracks with technical scree traverses, rock, compacted earth, switchbacks and long singletrack descents through Berber villages and pine forest. A documented one-way Oukaimeden to Asni route is about 33 km with roughly 1785 m of descent and 245 m of climbing; the nearby Asni network has about 37 km of mapped trail. Best for experienced, self-sufficient enduro riders.

Getting up / price
No dependable bike lift. Pedal, arrange a vehicle shuttle, or ride with a local guide from Marrakech. The winter ski lifts are not a bike-park uplift. Carry repair supplies, water and offline navigation; trails are unsigned and route conditions can change after storms or road works.

⚠️ Remote natural mountain terrain with exposure, livestock and pedestrians. Do not ride blindly through villages or cultivated land, and use a local guide for the larger point-to-point descents.

Open season
Open from 1 April; closed from 1 December (typical riding window). Snow can linger at altitude in winter, while midsummer is very hot lower in the valleys; spring and autumn are usually best.

Singletrack, downhill sections and jump/drop playgrounds around Dajianshr Mountain inside Kenting National Park. Open coastal terrain with ocean views makes this Taiwan's most scenic trail zone, but heat, sun exposure and typhoon risk require planning.

A rough valley road and connecting tracks enter a deep volcanic canyon through rainforest, river crossings and waterfall country. It is scenic backcountry and expedition-style riding, not a signed singletrack park.

Four downhill, all-mountain and XC routes total about 10 km between Cota 1400 and the lower gondola, including Easy Breezy and Fairy Trail. The upper Cota 2000 sector is not part of the prepared MTB network.

Getting up / price
Sinaia gondola section 1000-1400 provides bike uplift. Check the daily cableway programme and bike tariff before riding.

Open season
Typical May-October operation, subject to gondola maintenance, wind and wet-trail closures.
Daily opening hours: 09:00-17:00
Typical summer estimate; check the official gondola programme.

Access
FromTransportDuration
BucharestTrain / car~1h45

Source: official Bike Resort Sinaia.

Ukraine's principal lift-served downhill park

Trails
One blue, two red and one black downhill trail use jumps, narrow bridges and natural forest obstacles. Lift 2 carries bicycles.

Getting up / price
2026 advertised adult price: UAH 800/day, UAH 550 half-day or UAH 350 single ride.

⚠️ Ukraine remains at war. Missile and drone attacks can occur in western regions; multiple governments advise against non-essential or all travel. Do not treat resort operation as evidence that travel is safe.

Open season
Summer operation is advertised, but dates and security conditions can change without notice.
Daily opening hours: 09:00-18:00
Published hours; security, curfew, weather and lift closures can override them.

Access
FromTransportDuration
Ivano-FrankivskCar / bus~2h

Sources: official Bukovel Bike Park and current Ukraine travel advice.

properties.name: Jonkershoek / Stellenbosch MTB (South Africa) [permit, no lift]

description.value:
World-class Cape mountain and winelands trail network

Trails
Long fire-road climbs feed rocky natural descents, flow trails, jumps and technical enduro lines around MTO Jonkershoek and the broader Stellenbosch network. The regional permit connects many neighbouring trail systems.

Getting up / price
No lift. Buy the correct day or regional permit before entering; the MTB network is on MTO land near, but administratively distinct from, the CapeNature reserve.

Open season
Rideable year-round, best in the cooler dry periods. Fire danger, forestry work and winter storms cause closures.

Access
FromTransportDuration
StellenboschBike / car~15 min
Cape TownCar~1h

Sources: Wine Lands Trails permit and Stellenbosch Trail Fund.

properties.name: Karkloof Country Club MTB (South Africa) [permit, no lift]

description.value:
Major KwaZulu-Natal plantation singletrack network

Trails
More than 300 km of riding crosses forestry land, river valleys and waterfall country. Marked loops range from short family rides to 55 km, with advanced optional features inside easier routes.

Getting up / price
No lift. Day visitors must start at Karkloof Country Club, pay before riding, sign the indemnity and display the issued bike board. Private-land vehicle drops are prohibited.

Open season
Open year-round subject to forestry, fire and weather closures.

Access
FromTransportDuration
HowickCar~20 min
DurbanCar~1h30

Source: official visitor and permit rules.

properties.name: Afriski Mountain MTB (Lesotho) [no summer lift confirmed]

description.value:
High-altitude Maloti Mountain riding above 3,000 m

Trails
Natural and built lines around Afriski include short flow and downhill trails such as Break Back Mountain and Bosman's Way, with broader highland tracks extending toward Mahlasela Pass. Thin air, rock and severe weather make even short rides demanding.

Getting up / price
No summer bike uplift is currently confirmed. Pedal, arrange resort transport or ride as part of an organized event; do not assume the winter ski lift carries bikes.

Open season
Best September-May outside the main snow season. Storms, snow and high winds can occur at any time.

Access
FromTransportDuration
Butha-ButheCar~2h
JohannesburgCar~5h

Sources: Visit Lesotho and current mapped Afriski trails. Check border, road and resort status.

properties.name: Virgin Freeride / Red Bull Rampage Zone [no lift]

description.value:
Virgin Freeride / Red Bull Rampage Zone - Virgin, UT

Trails
Flying Monkey is the documented public expert descent from the southern rim of Smith Mesa north of Virgin: 2.53 miles of narrow, steep and loose trail with sharp turns, jumps, unavoidable obstacles, sudden drop-offs and extreme exposure. It runs through the same broader red-desert freeride landscape used by Red Bull Rampage. Historic and current Rampage competition lines are separate, invitation-only event terrain; do not treat them as public trails.

Getting up / price
No lift. Pedal the Mesa Road / Flying Monkey access roads or arrange a vehicle drop where legal; the BLM recommends leaving vehicles before the access road becomes rough.

⚠️ Flying Monkey is rated extremely difficult by the BLM. It has 20% or steeper grades, crumbling surfaces and places where a mistake could cause serious injury or death. There are no convenient places to stop or turn around.

Open season
Best from mid-September to mid-May. Avoid wet clay, summer heat and active event or land-management closures.

Access
FromTransportDuration
VirginBike / car~15 min to Mesa Road

Sources: BLM Flying Monkey trail description, access and safety guidance and Red Bull Rampage event information. Trail status and access can change; verify before travel.

Mapped 2.3 km central descent of the BLM's 2.53-mile extremely difficult Flying Monkey trail. Narrow, loose and exposed terrain with jumps, unavoidable obstacles, sharp turns and sudden drop-offs. Source: OpenStreetMap way 1101932075 (ODbL).

Moab - The Whole Enchilada - Moab, UT

Trails
A landmark high-alpine-to-desert enduro descent linking Burro Pass, Hazard County, Kokopelli, UPS, LPS and Porcupine Rim. Snow and extreme heat make timing essential.

Trails
The Silvretta Bike Arena Ischgl/Samnaun is a major commercial lift-served gravity area with around 100 km of marked trails, from easy flow lines to technical high-alpine descents. Notable runs include the Velill Trail, Zeblastrail, Schmuggler Trail, Flimjoch Trail and Greitspitz Grat Trail. The arena links Ischgl in Austria with Samnaun in Switzerland and is part of the Gravity Card network. Trail grades range from blue (easy) through red (intermediate) to black (expert).

The main uplift is the Silvrettabahn gondola from Ischgl village to Idalp. The Fimbabahn runs parallel from a nearby valley station, and the Flimjochbahn continues from Idalp to Viderjoch for the cross-border and higher trails. Bike transport is permitted on all operating gondolas and chairlifts. The 2026 adult "Bike Unlimited" day pass is EUR 42.00; the Smuggler Ticket biker unlimited (cross-border) is EUR 60.50.

Trails
Eleven signed BTT routes spread across the resort, mostly dropping from the two bike chairlifts. Two chairlifts carry bikes: the TSD Clot der Os and the TSD Bosque. The day bike pass gives unlimited ascents and descents on both lifts. Adult day pass 30 EUR; child (born 2015-2023) 20 EUR. Multi-day bike passes and a July-August BaqueiraPASS Summer are also sold.

properties.name: Madonna di Campiglio / Pinzolo Bike Area (Italy) [22 EUR]

description.value:
Pradalago 2102 m - top of the Pradalago gondola

Trails
Lift-served bike area in the Brenta Dolomites around Madonna di Campiglio and Pinzolo. The area links 14 lift systems with bike transport, with 8 downhill trails (approx. 29 km), 13 enduro trails (approx. 206 km) and a large network of cross-country and e-bike routes. Named descents include Fogajard, Sentiero dell'Orso, Trail Cavradoss, Margun Degre and the tracciato downhill Tosa. The Pinzolo side (Doss Bike Area, formerly Brenta Bike Park) has been redesigned around beginner-friendly natural trails and a skill park.

Getting up / price
The area sells per-ride tickets rather than an unlimited day pass. Adult return ticket for the main Campiglio uplifts (Pradalago / 5 Laghi / Spinale) is 22 EUR (27 EUR during high season 25 July - 30 August); bike transport supplement is 5 EUR. Online purchase discounts up to 15%. Children up to 8 years ride free.

Open season
Madonna di Campiglio lifts: 18 June - 20 September 2026. Pinzolo lifts: 20 June - 13 September 2026. Daily hours generally 08:30 - 17:20, with reduced midday closure at the start/end of season.

Sandy Ridge 320 m - main trailhead of the Sandy Ridge Trail System

Trails
BLM describes about 17 miles of directional, downhill-only singletrack designed for mountain bikers in the Cascade foothills west of Mount Hood. The range runs from machine-built beginner flow trails with rollers and table tops to double-black expert lines with exposure, rock gardens, steep grades and jump lines. Mapped named descents include Hide and Seek, Follow The Leader, Quid Pro Flow, Communication Breakdown, Two Turntables and a Microwave, Flow Motion, Rock Drop, Johnny Royale, TNT, Little Monkey and Laura's Loop.

Getting up / price
No lift. The system is pedal-accessed: ride up the gated Homestead Road (paved, roughly 3-4 miles) to the upper trailhead. A parking pass is required at the main lot: $5/day for a passenger car, $10 for a van, $20 for a bus, or $30/year Northwest Oregon District pass. Buy at the kiosk or via Recreation.gov.

Open season
Open year-round, dawn to dusk. The access road and upper trails can be snow-covered in mid-winter; the trails generally hold up well in wet conditions.

description.value:
Pedal-accessed freeride and enduro trail network above Hood River at ~321 m

Trails
About 25 mi / 40 km of singletrack ranging from mellow flow to expert wooden features. Notable trails include Seven Streams, Family Man skills park, Grand Prix, Bad Motor Scooter, Charley's Loop, Mitchell Ridge, Mobius, 140 Trail, Kleeway, Float On, Spaghetti Factory, Thee Way, Cardiac Bypass and Donkey Boy. Rides best as a clockwise loop; the lower canyon is beginner-friendly while the upper forest holds the freeride lines.

Getting up / price
No lift. Pedal up or arrange a local shuttle. A Hood River County Forest parking permit is required at Seven Streams, Post Flats, Family Man, Binns Hill, Kingsley and Pinemont staging areas: $45 annual / $10 daily (effective July 2026), available online and from local vendors.

Open season
Open from 01 January; closed from 31 December (ridable year-round, best spring-fall). Summers are dry; winters are wet and muddy. Fire-season restrictions can close motorized access and sometimes trails; check current regulations before visiting.

Purpose-built freeride and DH lines on Mt. Brown in the Coast Range. description.value:
Camp Tamarancho trailhead at 230 m - permit-based natural singletrack in Marin County

Trails
An ~11-mile loop of hand-built, bike-legal singletrack on Boy Scouts of America property west of Fairfax. The clockwise loop climbs Alchemist Trail (uphill only as of 2026), then Goldman, Serpentine, Wagon Wheel and B-17 trails. Broken Dam Trail closes the loop. Endor Trail is a short, downhill-only flow trail with high berms and jumps; Caballo Rojo is another downhill-only option. Expect roots, rocks, switchbacks and the famous rock on Serpentine; Wagon Wheel adds rock gardens. Difficulty ranges from beginner-friendly sections to intermediate/advanced, with a few expert features.

Getting up / price
No lift. Park in Fairfax and ride ~1.5 miles up Iron Springs Road to the trailhead kiosk. A permit is required and must be visible while riding. Day pass $6; annual single $50; family annual $75; Gold single $95; Gold family $135. Buy online from the Marin Council, BSA, or get day passes in person at Sunshine Bicycle Center in Fairfax. Class-1 eMTB only; no dogs; no riding when wet or muddy; no parking on Iron Springs Road.

Open season
Open year-round; closed when trails are wet, raining or muddy after storms.

Pedal-accessed Bay Area trail system from sea level to ~320 m on San Pablo Bay

Trails
About 15 miles of multi-use trails wind through oak woodland, salt marsh and grassland. The Turtle Back Nature Trail is an easy, hiker-only ADA loop. For bikes, the Shoreline/Bayview Loop (6.9 mi, moderate) is the classic circuit, while Bay View/Bay Hills/Back Ranch Fire Trail (5.6 mi, strenuous) climbs San Pedro Mountain to ~320 m with views of Mount Tamalpais, Mount Diablo and the Coast Range. Terrain ranges from mellow fire road to rocky, rutted descents.

Getting up / price
No lift. Pedal up on park roads and fire roads. Vehicle day-use fee is $5 per car; annual California State Parks passes are accepted. Friends of China Camp annual pass/membership also available.

Open season
Open year-round, 8 a.m. to sunset daily. Coastal-temperate climate: winter ~10-15 C, summer ~20-30 C; mornings can be foggy.
Class I pedal-assist e-bikes only, max 15 mph (5 mph on blind corners and when passing). Dogs are not allowed on trails.

properties.name: Skeggs Point / El Corte de Madera Creek Preserve [no lift]

description.value:
Skeggs Point 709 m - trailhead

Trails
El Corte de Madera Creek Preserve, locally called Skeggs Point, is a 2,908-acre redwood-forest network with 34+ miles of multi-use trail (about 20 miles singletrack and 14 miles fire road). Bike-legal highlights include Sierra Morena, Oljon, Resolution, North Leaf, Manzanita, Giant Salamander, Blue Blossom, Fir, Methuselah and Timberview. Difficulty ranges from mellow intermediate singletrack to steep, technical, rocky sections that many riders hike-a-bike; Fir Trail and some others are really only fun downhill. Helmets are required, the trail speed limit is 15 mph, and e-bikes are not allowed. Check current trail status before riding, as some trails close seasonally for wet weather or salamander protection.

Getting up / price
No lift - every climb is earned. Park free at the Skeggs Point vista-point lot (26 spaces, across Skyline Blvd from the trailhead) or at the El Corte de Madera Parking Area (65 spaces, about 0.4 mi south). Restrooms are available at the main El Corte de Madera lot. Bring a map or GPS; the dense network is easy to get lost in.

Open season
Open a half-hour before sunrise until a half-hour after sunset, year-round. Expect heavy coastal fog and winter wet-weather closures, especially on Giant Salamander Trail. Verify current conditions on the Midpen website before heading out.

properties.name: Trione-Annadel State Park (Santa Rosa, CA) [no lift]

description.value:
Channel Drive entrance, ~120 m (~400 ft)

Trails
Pedal-accessed state park with 35-45 miles of multi-use trails through volcanic rock, basalt outcrops and old cobblestone quarry terrain. Riding mixes oak woodland, grassland, chaparral and riparian zones. Lake Ilsanjo and Ledson Marsh sit inside the park; Bennett Mountain tops out at 575 m (1,887 ft). Popular routes include the Canyon Trail, South Burma and ridges above Lake Ilsanjo. Natural, rocky and loose volcanic surfaces mean the riding suits confident intermediates and experts; a few easier fire roads and the Channel Trail are more beginner-friendly.

Getting up / price
No lift. You pedal up the fire roads and ridge trails. Vehicle day-use fee is $8 (regular auto) paid at the Visitor Center on Channel Drive or via the LAZ app; several California State Parks annual passes are accepted. No camping inside the park; nearest camping is Spring Lake Regional Park and Sugarloaf Ridge State Park. E-bikes are considered motorized vehicles and are not allowed on trails.

Open season
Open year-round 8 AM to sunset, no overnight use. Best riding is spring through fall; summers are warm and winters are cool and muddy after rain. Peak wildflower season is April to June.
